work.text: One of its feet, livid and scarred with the nails, touches at the foot of the cross the naked shoulder of the Magdalen. It does not bear upon, it lightly brushes it. The contact cannot be perceived ; it is divined rather than seen.

source.author: Eugène Fromentin
source.title: The Old Masters of Belgium and Holland (Les Maîtres d'autrefois), trans. Mary C. Robbins

work.text: Altarpieces such as The Raising of the Cross (1610) and The Descent from the Cross (1611–1614) for the Cathedral of Our Lady in Antwerp were particularly important in establishing Rubens as Flanders' leading painter shortly after his return.

moment.text: Rubens, by a somewhat subtle extension of the Greek name Christophoros … determined to introduce into his picture all the persons who … had borne Christ during the course of his earthly existence.
moment.lead: Commissioned by the Guild of Arquebusiers, whose patron was St Christopher:

source.author: Émile Michel
source.title: Rubens: His Life, His Work, and His Time, vol. 1, trans. Elizabeth Lee

matters.text: It is probable that this fair girl with the dark eyes, firm look, and clean-cut profile is a portrait … one of Isabel Brandt, whom he had married two years before

source.author: Eugène Fromentin
source.title: The Old Masters of Belgium and Holland (Les Maîtres d'autrefois), trans. Mary C. Robbins

matters.text: the deans paid three visits to the painter's studio, not only to see the progress the work was making, but also to satisfy themselves of the quality of the panels employed, to make sure that the wood was quite “sound and free from sap.” … According to custom, the Guild presented Isabella Brant with a pair of gloves
